newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat's Lancia launches two new models.
newsitem.headline: Fiat's Lancia launches two new models.

text.p: Fiat Auto said it was poised to beef up its upmarket Lancia range with the launch of a coupe version of its Kappa model and two new-engine versions of the subcompact Ypsilon.

Giancarlo Perlo, Lancia product manager, said 500 billion lire had been invested in a new production line at the Termoli plant in Southern Italy which will build a 16-valve variant of the "Fire" engine model.
The Lancia Kappa coupe, produced at Chivasso in Northwest Italy will go on sale at the beginning of April in Switzerland.

The Kappa will go on sale in Italy in the second half of May before its launch in the rest of Europe. Some 1,500 are expected to be produced this year, eventually rising to 3,000 a year, half of them for sale abroad.
The Kappa's price has still to be announced.

The Ypsilon models, powered by a new 1,242 cc 16-valve Fire unit or a 1,108 cc version, go on sale on April 15 and 25,000 of each version are expected to be sold annually in Europe. Prices of the new Ypsilon models are expected to range from 18.1 million lire for the 1,108 cc version to 22.3-22.6 million lire for the 1,242 cc variant. -- Milan newsroom +392-66102321
